questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its prorogation.
2. A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha, which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha, shall not lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Prorogation only ends a session; under Article 107 no Bill lapses because of it, so 1 is wrong. A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha that the Lok Sabha has not passed survives dissolution of the Lok Sabha, so 2 is right.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q1

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are the indicator/indicators used by IFPRI to compute the Global Hunger Index Report?
1. Undernourishment
2. Child stunting
3. Child mortality
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Global Hunger Index uses four indicators: undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting and child mortality. All three listed items are among them.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q2

questions.q:
There has been a persistent deficit budget year after year. Which action/actions of the following can be taken by the Government to reduce the deficit?
1. Reducing revenue expenditure
2. Introducing new welfare schemes
3. Rationalizing subsidies
4. Reducing import duty
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: A deficit shrinks only if spending falls or receipts rise. Cutting revenue expenditure and rationalising subsidies reduce spending; new welfare schemes add spending and lower import duty cuts revenue.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q3

questions.q:
The establishment of 'Payment Banks' is being allowed in India to promote financial inclusion. Which of the following statements is/are correct in this context?
1. Mobile telephone companies and supermarket chains that are owned and controlled by residents are eligible to be promoters of Payment Banks.
2. Payment Banks can issue both credit cards and debit cards.
3. Payment Banks cannot undertake lending activities.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: RBI's 2014 guidelines name resident-owned mobile companies and supermarket chains as eligible promoters, and bar payments banks from lending. They may issue debit/ATM cards but not credit cards, so 2 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q4

questions.q:
With reference to 'LiFi', recently in the news, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It uses light as the medium for high-speed data transmission.
2. It is a wireless technology and is several times faster than 'WiFi'.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Li-Fi sends data by flickering LED light too fast for the eye to notice. It is wireless like Wi-Fi but uses visible light instead of radio waves and has shown much higher speeds.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q5

questions.q: The term 'Intended Nationally Determined Contributions' is sometimes seen in the news in the context of
o: pledges made by the European countries to rehabilitate refugees from the war-affected Middle East
plan of action outlined by the countries of the world to combat climate change
capital contributed by the member countries in the establishment of Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank
plan of action outlined by the countries of the world regarding Sustainable Development Goals
questions.e: INDCs were the climate action plans countries submitted under the UNFCCC before the 2015 Paris conference. Under the Paris Agreement they became NDCs.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q6

questions.q: Which one of the following is a purpose of 'UDAY', a scheme of the Government?
o: Providing technical and financial assistance to start-up entrepreneurs in the field of renewable sources of energy
Providing electricity to every household in the country by 2018
Replacing the coal-based power plants with natural gas, nuclear, solar, wind and tidal power plants over a period of time
Providing for financial turnaround and revival of power distribution companies
questions.e: UDAY (2015) was a rescue package for loss-making state power distribution companies: states took over most DISCOM debt and DISCOMs committed to cut losses. Its aim was their financial turnaround.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q7

questions.q:
With reference to 'IFC Masala Bonds', sometimes seen in the news, which of the statements given below is/are correct?
1. The International Finance Corporation, which offers these bonds, is an arm of the World Bank.
2. They are the rupee-denominated bonds and are a source of debt financing for the public and private sector.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Masala bonds are rupee-denominated bonds issued abroad, first by the International Finance Corporation, the World Bank Group's private-sector arm. They raise debt for public and private projects in India.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q8

questions.q:
Regarding the taxation system of Krishna Deva, the ruler of Vijayanagar, consider the following statements:
1. The tax rate on land was fixed depending on the quality of the land.
2. Private owners of workshops paid an industries tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Under Krishnadeva Raya land revenue varied with the quality of land and crop, and manufacturers and craftsmen paid taxes on their trade. Both statements are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q9

questions.q: Which one of the following books of ancient India has the love story of the son of the founder of Sunga dynasty?
questions.e: Pushyamitra founded the Sunga dynasty and his son was Agnimitra. Kalidasa's play Malavikagnimitra is about Agnimitra's love for Malavika.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q10

questions.q: In the context of which of the following do you sometimes find the terms 'amber box, blue box and green box' in the news?
questions.e: The WTO's Agreement on Agriculture sorts farm subsidies into boxes: green (allowed), amber (trade-distorting, to be reduced) and blue (linked to production limits).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q11

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are included in the capital budget of the Government of India?
1. Expenditure on acquisition of assets like roads, buildings, machinery, etc.
2. Loans received from foreign governments
3. Loans and advances granted to the States and Union Territories
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The capital budget has capital receipts (such as loans from foreign governments) and capital payments (asset creation and loans to States and UTs). All three items belong to it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q12

questions.q:
What is/are the importance/importances of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification?
1. It aims to promote effective action through innovative national programmes and supportive international partnerships.
2. It has a special/particular focus on South Asia and North Africa regions, and its Secretariat facilitates the allocation of major portion of financial resources to these regions.
3. It is committed to bottom-up approach, encouraging the participation of local people in combating the desertification.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The UNCCD works through national action programmes with international partnerships and stresses local participation (bottom-up). Its regional priority is Africa, not South Asia and North Africa.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q13

questions.q: Recently, which one of the following currencies has been proposed to be added to the basket of IMF's SDR?
questions.e: In November 2015 the IMF decided to add China's renminbi to the SDR basket as its fifth currency, effective October 2016.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q14

questions.q:
With reference to the International Monetary and Financial Committee (IMFC), consider the following statements:
1. IMFC discusses matters of concern affecting the global economy, and advises the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on the direction of its work.
2. The World Bank participates as observer in IMFC's meetings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The IMFC is the IMF's ministerial advisory committee; it discusses the world economy and guides the Fund's work. The World Bank attends its meetings as an observer.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q15

questions.q: 'Rashtriya Garima Abhiyaan' is a national campaign to
o: rehabilitate the homeless and destitute persons and provide them with suitable sources of livelihood
release the sex workers from their practice and provide them with alternative sources of livelihood
eradicate the practice of manual scavenging and rehabilitate the manual scavengers
release the bonded labourers from their bondage and rehabilitate them
questions.e: Rashtriya Garima Abhiyan ('dignity campaign') works to end manual scavenging and rehabilitate those engaged in it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q16

questions.q:
With reference to the cultural history of medieval India, consider the following statements:
1. Siddhas (Sittars) of Tamil region were monotheistic and condemned idolatry.
2. Lingayats of Kannada region questioned the theory of rebirth and rejected the caste hierarchy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Tamil Siddhas were monotheistic and attacked idol worship and ritual. The Lingayats of Karnataka rejected caste and questioned the theory of rebirth. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q17

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the term 'import cover', sometimes seen in the news?
o: It is the ratio of value of imports to the Gross Domestic Product of a country
It is the total value of imports of a country in a year
It is the ratio between the value of exports and that of imports between two countries
It is the number of months of imports that could be paid for by a country's international reserves
questions.e: Import cover is forex reserves divided by the average monthly import bill: the number of months of imports the reserves can pay for.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q18

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Community sometimes mentioned in the news In the affairs of
1. Kurd Bangladesh
2. Madhesi Nepal
3. Rohingya Myanmar
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Kurds live in Turkey, Iraq, Syria and Iran, not Bangladesh. Madhesis are in Nepal's Terai and Rohingyas in Myanmar's Rakhine state.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q19

questions.q:
With reference to 'Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW)', consider the following statements:
1. It is an organization of European Union in working relation with NATO and WHO.
2. It monitors chemical industry to prevent new weapons from emerging.
3. It provides assistance and protection to States (Parties) against chemical weapons threats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The OPCW in The Hague implements the Chemical Weapons Convention for states worldwide; it is not an EU body. It inspects chemical industry and helps members defend against chemical weapons.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q20

questions.q:
With reference to 'Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana', consider the following statements:
1. Under this scheme, farmers will have to pay a uniform premium of two percent for any crop they cultivate in any season of the year.
2. This scheme covers post-harvest losses arising out of cyclones and unseasonal rains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: PMFBY premiums are 2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops, so there is no uniform 2%. It does cover post-harvest losses from cyclones and unseasonal rain.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q21

questions.q: In which of the following regions of India are you most likely to come across the 'Great Indian Hornbill' in its natural habitat?
o: Higher Himalayas of Jammu and Kashmir
questions.e: The Great Hornbill needs tall evergreen forests for fruit and nesting holes. In India these are in the Western Ghats and the North-East.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q22

questions.q:
Which of the following are the key features of 'National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA)'?
1. River basin is the unit of planning and management.
2. It spearheads the river conservation efforts at the national level.
3. One of the Chief Ministers of the States through which the Ganga flows becomes the Chairman of NGRBA on rotation basis.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: NGRBA (2009) took the river basin as the unit of planning and led national Ganga conservation efforts. It was chaired by the Prime Minister, not by Chief Ministers in rotation.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q23

questions.q: Why does the Government of India promote the use of 'Neem-coated Urea' in agriculture?
o: Release of Neem oil in the soil increases nitrogen fixation by the soil microorganisms
Neem coating slows down the rate of dissolution of urea in the soil
Nitrous oxide, which is a greenhouse gas, is not at all released into atmosphere by crop fields
It is a combination of a weedicide and a fertilizer for particular crops
questions.e: Neem coating slows the release of nitrogen from urea, so more reaches the crop and less is lost. It also stops subsidised urea being diverted to industry.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q24

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chief Secretary in a State is appointed by the Governor of that State.
2. The Chief Secretary in a State has a fixed tenure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Chief Secretary is chosen by the Chief Minister; orders are issued in the Governor's name only formally. The post has no fixed tenure, which the 2nd ARC recommended changing.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q25

questions.q:
With reference to 'Stand Up India Scheme', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Its purpose is to promote entrepreneurship among SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.
2. It provides for refinance through SIDBI.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Stand Up India backs bank loans to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs for new enterprises, with refinance through SIDBI. Both statements are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q26

questions.q:
The FAO accords the status of 'Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS)' to traditional agricultural systems. What is the overall goal of this initiative?
1. To provide modern technology, training in modern farming methods and financial support to local communities of identified GIAHS so as to greatly enhance their agricultural productivity
2. To identify and safeguard eco-friendly traditional farm practices and their associated landscapes, agricultural biodiversity and knowledge systems of the local communities
3. To provide Geographical Indication status to all the varieties of agricultural produce in such identified GIAHS
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: FAO's GIAHS programme recognises and protects traditional farming systems, their landscapes, agro-biodiversity and knowledge. It does not modernise them or grant GI tags.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q27

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are tributary/tributaries of Brahmaputra?
1. Dibang
2. Kameng
3. Lohit
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Dibang and Lohit join the Siang from the left to form the Brahmaputra, and the Kameng joins from the right in Assam. All three are tributaries.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q28

questions.q:
The term 'Core Banking Solutions' is sometimes seen in the news. Which of the following statements best describes/describe this term?
1. It is a networking of a bank's branches which enables customers to operate their accounts from any branch of the bank on its network regardless of where they open their accounts.
2. It is an effort to increase RBI's control over commercial banks through computerization.
3. It is a detailed procedure by which a bank with huge non-performing assets is taken over by another bank.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Core Banking Solutions links all branches to a central system, so customers can bank at any branch. It is not an RBI control tool or a merger procedure.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q29

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Terms sometimes seen in the news Their origin
1. Annex–I Countries Cartagena Protocol
2. Certified Emissions Reductions Nagoya Protocol
3. Clean Development Mechanism Kyoto Protocol
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Annex I countries are a UNFCCC category; Certified Emission Reductions come from the Kyoto Protocol's CDM. Cartagena and Nagoya Protocols belong to the CBD. Only pair 3 is right.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q30

questions.q: In the context of the developments in Bioinformatics, the term 'transcriptome', sometimes seen in the news, refers to
o: a range of enzymes used in genome editing
the full range of mRNA molecules expressed by an organism
the description of the mechanism of gene expression
a mechanism of genetic mutations taking place in cells
questions.e: The transcriptome is the complete set of RNA (mainly mRNA) transcripts expressed by an organism or cell, just as the genome is its full DNA.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q31

questions.q: 'Mission Indradhanush' launched by the Government of India pertains to
o: immunization of children and pregnant women
construction of smart cities across the country
India's own search for the Earth-like planets in outer space
questions.e: Mission Indradhanush (2014) is a catch-up drive to fully immunise children and pregnant women in low-coverage areas.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q32

questions.q:
Which of the following best describes/describe the aim of 'Green India Mission' of the Government of India?
1. Incorporating environmental benefits and costs into the Union and State Budgets thereby implementing the 'green accounting'
2. Launching the second green revolution to enhance agricultural output so as to ensure food security to one and all in the future
3. Restoring and enhancing forest cover and responding to climate change by a combination of adaptation and mitigation measures
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Green India Mission, one of eight NAPCC missions, aims to protect and expand forest cover and respond to climate change through adaptation and mitigation.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q33

questions.q:
With reference to pre-packaged items in India, it is mandatory to the manufacturer to put which of the following information on the main label, as per the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011?
1. List of ingredients including additives
2. Nutrition information
3. Recommendations, if any, made by the medical profession about the possibility of any allergic reactions
4. Vegetarian/non-vegetarian
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: FSSAI's 2011 labelling rules required ingredients (with additives), nutrition information and the veg/non-veg mark. A medical statement on allergic reactions was not mandatory.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q34

questions.q: 'Project Loon', sometimes seen in the news, is related to
questions.e: Project Loon used high-altitude balloons as floating relay stations to provide internet to remote areas: a wireless communication technology.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q35

questions.q: 'Net metering' is sometimes seen in the news in the context of promoting the
o: production and use of solar energy by the households/consumers
use of piped natural gas in the kitchens of households
installation of CNG kits in motorcars
installation of water meters in urban households
questions.e: Net metering lets rooftop solar users export surplus power to the grid and pay only for the net power drawn. It encourages household solar.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q36

questions.q: India’s ranking in the ‘Ease of Doing Business Index’ is sometimes seen in the news. Which of the following has declared that ranking?
o: Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD)
questions.e: The Ease of Doing Business ranking was published by the World Bank in its Doing Business reports.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q37

questions.q: Banjaras during the medieval period of Indian history were generally
questions.e: Banjaras were nomadic traders who carried grain and goods in caravans of pack animals; Alauddin Khalji and the Mughals used them to supply markets and armies.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q38

questions.q: Who of the following had first deciphered the edicts of Emperor Ashoka?
questions.e: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837-38, which made Ashoka's edicts readable.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q39

questions.q:
With reference to the ‘Gram Nyayalaya Act’, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. As per the Act, Gram Nyayalayas can hear only civil cases and not criminal cases.
2. The Act allows local social activists as mediators/reconciliators.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Gram Nyayalayas hear both civil and criminal cases, so 1 is wrong. The Act lets village-level social workers act as conciliators, so 2 is right.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q40
questions.u: Justice Administration, Law Enforcement & Statutory Frameworks

questions.q:
With reference to the ‘Trans-Pacific Partnership’, consider the following statements:
1. It is an agreement among all the Pacific Rim countries except China and Russia.
2. It is a strategic alliance for the purpose of maritime security only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The TPP was a trade agreement signed by 12 Pacific Rim countries in 2016, not all except China and Russia, and not a maritime security pact. Neither statement holds.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q41

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: The India-Africa Summit
1. held in 2015 was the third such Summit
2. was actually initiated by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1951
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The India-Africa Forum Summits were held in 2008, 2011 and 2015, so 2015 was the third. They were not started by Nehru in 1951.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q42

questions.q:
What is/are the purpose/purposes of the ‘Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR)’ announced by RBI?
1. These guidelines help improve the transparency in the methodology followed by banks for determining the interest rates on advances.
2. These guidelines help ensure availability of bank credit at interest rates which are fair to the borrowers as well as the banks.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: RBI introduced MCLR in 2016 to make banks' lending-rate setting more transparent and to ensure credit at rates fair to both borrowers and banks.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q43

questions.q:
What is/are unique about ‘Kharai camel’, a breed found in India?
1. It is capable of swimming up to three kilometres in seawater.
2. It survives by grazing on mangroves.
3. It lives in the wild and cannot be domesticated.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Kharai camel of Kutch swims through seawater to reach and graze on mangroves. It is a domesticated breed kept by herders, so 3 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q44

questions.q: Recently, our scientists have discovered a new and distinct species of banana plant which attains a height of about 11 metres and has orange-coloured fruit pulp. In which part of India has it been discovered?
questions.e: Musa indandamanensis, a wild banana about 11 m tall with orange pulp, was found in Little Andaman in the Andaman Islands.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q45

questions.q: Which one of the following is the best description of ‘INS Astradharini’, that was in the news recently?
questions.e: INS Astradharini, commissioned in 2015, is an indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel used for underwater weapon trials.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q46

questions.q: What is ‘Greased Lightning–10 (GL–10)’, recently in the news?
o: Solar-powered two-seater aircraft designed by Japan
questions.e: GL-10 'Greased Lightning' is a NASA battery-powered aircraft with ten electric motors that takes off vertically and flies like a plane.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q47

questions.q:
With reference to 'Initiative for Nutritional Security through Intensive Millets Promotion', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. This initiative aims to demonstrate the improved production and post-harvest technologies, and to demonstrate value addition techniques, in an integrated manner, with cluster approach.
2. Poor, small, marginal and tribal farmers have larger stake in this scheme.
3. An important objective of the scheme is to encourage farmers of commercial crops to shift to millet cultivation by offering them free kits of critical inputs of nutrients and microirrigation equipment.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: INSIMP demonstrated improved millet production and processing in clusters, and small, marginal and tribal farmers who grow millets benefit most. It did not aim to shift commercial-crop farmers.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q48

questions.q: The 'Swadeshi' and 'Boycott' were adopted as methods of struggle for the first time during the
o: agitation against the Partition of Bengal
visit of the Simon Commission to India
questions.e: Swadeshi and boycott were first used as mass methods in the agitation against the 1905 Partition of Bengal.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q49

questions.q:
With reference to the religious history of India, consider the following statements:
1. The concept of Bodhisattva is central to Hinayana sect of Buddhism.
2. Bodhisattva is a compassionate one on his way to enlightenment.
3. Bodhisattva delays achieving his own salvation to help all sentient beings on their path to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Bodhisattva ideal belongs to Mahayana, not Hinayana. A Bodhisattva is a compassionate being who delays his own nirvana to help others reach it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q50

questions.q: 'Doctors Without Borders (Medecins Sans Frontieres)', often in the news, is
o: a division of World Health Organization
an inter-governmental agency sponsored by European Union
a specialized agency of the United Nations
questions.e: Médecins Sans Frontières, founded in France in 1971, is an independent international medical NGO, not part of the UN, WHO or EU.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q51

questions.q:
With reference to an initiative called 'The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB)', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is an initiative hosted by UNEP, IMF and World Economic Forum.
2. It is a global initiative that focuses on drawing attention to the economic benefits of biodiversity.
3. It presents an approach that can help decision-makers recognize, demonstrate and capture the value of ecosystems and biodiversity.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: TEEB is hosted by UNEP (not the IMF or WEF). It highlights the economic value of biodiversity and helps decision-makers recognise and capture it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q52

questions.q:
With reference to 'Red Sanders', sometimes seen in the news, consider the following statements:
1. It is a tree species found in a part of South India.
2. It is one of the most important trees in the tropical rain forest areas of South India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Red Sanders is endemic to the southern Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh. It grows in dry deciduous forest, not tropical rainforest.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q53

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct? Proper design and effective implementation of UN-REDD+ Programme can significantly contribute to
1. protection of biodiversity
2. resilience of forest ecosystems
3. poverty reduction
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Well-designed REDD+ action can protect biodiversity, make forests more resilient and reduce poverty, besides cutting emissions. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q54

questions.q: What is 'Greenhouse Gas Protocol'?
o: It is an international accounting tool for government and business leaders to understand, quantify and manage greenhouse gas emissions
It is an initiative of the United Nations to offer financial incentives to developing countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and to adopt eco-friendly technologies
It is inter-governmental agreement ratified by all the member countries of the United Nations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to specified levels by the year 2022
It is one of the multilateral REDD+ initiatives hosted by the World Bank
questions.e: The GHG Protocol, developed by WRI and WBCSD, is the standard accounting tool businesses and governments use to measure and manage emissions. It is not a treaty or UN programme.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q55

questions.q:
With reference to 'Financial Stability and Development Council', consider the following statements:
1. It is an organ of NITI Aayog.
2. It is headed by the Union Finance Minister.
3. It monitors macroprudential supervision of the economy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The FSDC is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and oversees macro-prudential supervision of the economy. It is not part of NITI Aayog.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q56

questions.q:
With reference to 'Agenda 21', sometimes seen in the news, consider the following statements:
1. It is a global action plan for sustainable development.
2. It originated in the World Summit on Sustainable Development held in Johannesburg in 2002.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Agenda 21 is the global action plan for sustainable development adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, not at Johannesburg in 2002.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q57

questions.q: Satya Shodhak Samaj organized
o: a movement for upliftment of tribals in Bihar
questions.e: Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 in Maharashtra to fight caste discrimination.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q58

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct? Viruses can infect
1. bacteria
2. fungi
3. plants
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Viruses infect all cellular life: bacteriophages attack bacteria, mycoviruses fungi, and viruses like TMV plants.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q59

questions.q: The term 'Base Erosion and Profit Shifting' is sometimes seen in the news in the context of
o: mining operation by multinational companies in resource-rich but backward areas
curbing of the tax evasion by multinational companies
exploitation of genetic resources of a country by multinational companies
lack of consideration of environmental costs in the planning and implementation of developmental projects
questions.e: BEPS refers to multinationals shifting profits to low-tax places to avoid tax. The OECD/G20 BEPS project aims to curb it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q60

questions.q: Recently, India's first 'National Investment and Manufacturing Zone' was proposed to be set up in
questions.e: Prakasam in Andhra Pradesh was among the first National Investment and Manufacturing Zones to get final approval.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q61

questions.q:
What is/are the purpose/purposes of 'District Mineral Foundations' in India?
1. Promoting mineral exploration activities in mineral-rich districts
2. Protecting the interests of the persons affected by mining operations
3. Authorizing State Governments to issue licences for mineral exploration
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: District Mineral Foundations are trusts funded by miners to benefit people and areas affected by mining. Exploration is handled by a separate trust, and licences are not their job.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q62

questions.q: 'SWAYAM', an initiative of the Government of India, aims at
o: promoting the Self Help Groups in rural areas
providing financial and technical assistance to young start-up entrepreneurs
promoting the education and health of adolescent girls
providing affordable and quality education to the citizens for free
questions.e: SWAYAM is the government's online course platform offering quality education free to all learners.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q63

questions.q: The Montague-Chelmsford Proposals were related to
questions.e: The Montagu-Chelmsford proposals led to the constitutional reforms of the Government of India Act 1919, including dyarchy in the provinces.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q64

questions.q:
What is/are common to the two historical places known as Ajanta and Mahabalipuram?
1. Both were built in the same period.
2. Both belong to the same religious denomination.
3. Both have rock-cut monuments.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: None of the statements given above is correct
questions.e: Ajanta (Buddhist, 2nd c. BCE to 5th c. CE) and Mahabalipuram (Pallava, Hindu, 7th-8th c.) differ in period and religion. Their only common feature is rock-cut monuments.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q65

questions.q:
With reference to 'Bitcoins', sometimes seen in the news, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Bitcoins are tracked by the Central Banks of the countries.
2. Anyone with a Bitcoin address can send and receive Bitcoins from anyone else with a Bitcoin address.
3. Online payments can be sent without either side knowing the identity of the other.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Bitcoin is a peer-to-peer virtual currency not issued or tracked by any central bank. Anyone with an address can transact, and parties can remain anonymous.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q66

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. New Development Bank has been set up by APEC.
2. The headquarters of New Development Bank is in Shanghai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The New Development Bank was set up by the BRICS countries, not APEC. Its headquarters is in Shanghai.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q67

questions.q: 'Gadgil Committee Report' and 'Kasturirangan Committee Report', sometimes seen in the news, are related to
questions.e: The Gadgil panel (2011) and the Kasturirangan group (2013) both dealt with protecting the ecology of the Western Ghats.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q68

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Calcutta Unitarian Committee
2. Tabernacle of New Dispensation
3. Indian Reform Association Keshab Chandra Sen is associated with the establishment of which of the above?
questions.e: Keshab Chandra Sen founded the Indian Reform Association (1870) and the Church of the New Dispensation (1881). The Calcutta Unitarian Committee (1821) was founded by Rammohun Roy and William Adam.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q69

questions.q: Which of the following is not a member of 'Gulf Cooperation Council'?
questions.e: The GCC's six members are Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Iran is not a member.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q70

questions.q:
What is/are the purpose/purposes of Government's 'Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme' and 'Gold Monetization Scheme'?
1. To bring the idle gold lying with Indian households into the economy
2. To promote FDI in the gold and jewellery sector
3. To reduce India's dependence on gold imports
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Both gold schemes aim to bring idle household gold into productive use and reduce gold imports. They have nothing to do with FDI.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q71

questions.q: 'Belt and Road Initiative' is sometimes mentioned in the news in the context of the affairs of
questions.e: The Belt and Road Initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, is China's project to connect Asia, Europe and Africa by land and sea routes.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q72

questions.q: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana is aimed at
o: bringing the small entrepreneurs into formal financial system
providing loans to poor farmers for cultivating particular crops
providing pensions to old and destitute persons
funding the voluntary organizations involved in the promotion of skill development and employment generation
questions.e: MUDRA gives small loans (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun) to micro enterprises outside the formal banking system, bringing them into formal finance.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q73

questions.q:
In which of the following regions of India are shale gas resources found?
1. Cambay Basin
2. Cauvery Basin
3. Krishna-Godavari Basin
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Cambay, Cauvery and Krishna-Godavari basins are all assessed to hold shale gas.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q74

questions.q: 'Global Financial Stability Report' is prepared by the
o: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
questions.e: The Global Financial Stability Report is published twice a year by the IMF.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q75

questions.q:
Regarding 'Atal Pension Yojana', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is minimum guaranteed pension scheme mainly targeted at unorganized sector workers.
2. Only one member of a family can join the scheme.
3. Same amount of pension is guaranteed for the spouse for life after subscriber's death.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Atal Pension Yojana gives a guaranteed pension mainly to unorganised workers, and the same pension continues to the spouse. Any eligible member of a family may join, so 2 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q76

questions.q: The term 'Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership' often appears in the news in the context of the affairs of a group of countries known as
questions.e: RCEP talks were launched in 2012 by the ten ASEAN members and their six free-trade partners, with ASEAN at the centre.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q77

questions.q:
On which of the following can you find the Bureau of Energy Efficiency Star Label?
1. Ceiling fans
2. Electric geysers
3. Tubular fluorescent lamps
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: BEE Star Labels cover tubular fluorescent lamps (mandatory) and ceiling fans and electric geysers (voluntary at the time). All three carry it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q78

questions.q: India is an important member of the 'International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor'. If this experiment succeeds, what is the immediate advantage for India?
o: It can use thorium in place of uranium for power generation
It can attain a global role in satellite navigation
It can drastically improve the efficiency of its fission reactors in power generation
It can build fusion reactors for power generation
questions.e: ITER is testing nuclear fusion at power-plant scale, and members share its results. Success would let India build fusion reactors for power.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q79

questions.q:
In the context of the history of India, consider the following pairs: Term Description
1. Eripatti Land, revenue from which was set apart for the maintenance of the village tank
2. Taniyurs Villages donated to a single Brahmin or a group of Brahmins
3. Ghatikas Colleges generally attached to the temples
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Eripatti was land whose revenue maintained the village tank, and ghatikas were colleges attached to temples. A taniyur was a large separate village; villages gifted to Brahmins were brahmadeyas.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q80

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The International Solar Alliance was launched at the United Nations Climate Change Conference in 2015.
2. The Alliance includes all the member countries of the United Nations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India and France launched the International Solar Alliance at COP21 in Paris in 2015. Membership is voluntary, not all UN members.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q81

questions.q: 'European Stability Mechanism', sometimes seen in the news, is an
o: agency created by EU to deal with the impact of millions of refugees arriving from Middle East
agency of EU that provides financial assistance to eurozone countries
agency of EU to deal with all the bilateral and multilateral agreements on trade
agency of EU to deal with the conflicts arising among the member countries
questions.e: The European Stability Mechanism is the euro area's permanent rescue fund, giving financial help to eurozone countries in distress.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q82

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are the advantage/advantages of practising drip irrigation?
1. Reduction in weed
2. Reduction in soil salinity
3. Reduction in soil erosion
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: None of the above is an advantage of practising drip irrigation
questions.e: Drip irrigation wets only the root zone, so fewer weeds grow and there is little runoff to erode soil. It does not reduce soil salinity; salts can build up at the edge of the wet zone.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q83

questions.q:
Regarding 'DigiLocker', sometimes seen in the news, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is a digital locker system offered by the Government under Digital India Programme.
2. It allows you to access your e-documents irrespective of your physical location.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: DigiLocker is a cloud document wallet under Digital India, so documents can be accessed from anywhere. Both statements are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q84

questions.q: Recently, linking of which of the following rivers was undertaken?
questions.e: In 2015 Godavari water reached the Krishna through the Polavaram right canal in Andhra Pradesh, the first river link of its kind.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q85

questions.q:
In the cities of our country, which among the following atmospheric gases are normally considered in calculating the value of Air Quality Index?
1. Carbon dioxide
2. Carbon monoxide
3. Nitrogen dioxide
4. Sulfur dioxide
5. Methane
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: India's AQI uses eight pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO₂, SO₂, CO, ozone, ammonia and lead. CO₂ and methane are not included.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q86

questions.q:
With reference to 'Astrosat', the astronomical observatory launched by India, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Other than USA and Russia, India is the only country to have launched a similar observatory into space.
2. Astrosat is a 2000 kg satellite placed in an orbit at 1650 km above the surface of the Earth.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: AstroSat weighed about 1,513 kg and orbits at 650 km. Other agencies such as ESA had launched space observatories before India, so neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q87

questions.q: With reference to the economic history of medieval India, the term 'Araghatta' refers to
o: land grants made to military officers
waterwheel used in the irrigation of land
questions.e: Araghatta was a water wheel used to lift water for irrigation.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q88

questions.q: With reference to the cultural history of India, the memorizing of chronicles, dynastic histories and epic tales was the profession of who of the following?
questions.e: The Magadhas, like the Sutas, were bards who memorised and recited chronicles, genealogies and epic tales. Shramanas and parivrajakas were ascetics.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q89

questions.q: Recently, for the first time in our country, which of the following States has declared a particular butterfly as 'State Butterfly'?
questions.e: Maharashtra became the first state to declare a state butterfly, the Blue Mormon, in 2015.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: The Mangalyaan launched by ISRO
1. is also called the Mars Orbiter Mission
2. made India the second country to have a spacecraft orbit the Mars after USA
3. made India the only country to be successful in making its spacecraft orbit the Mars in its very first attempt
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Mangalyaan is the Mars Orbiter Mission and India succeeded in its first attempt. India was the fourth space agency to reach Mars orbit, not second after the USA.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q91

questions.q: What was the main reason for the split in the Indian National Congress at Surat in 1907?
o: Introduction of communalism into Indian politics by Lord Minto
Extremists' lack of faith in the capacity of the moderates to negotiate with the British Government
Aurobindo Ghosh's inability to be elected as the President of the Indian National Congress
questions.e: The Surat split (1907) came because the Extremists lost faith in the Moderates' method of petitioning the British and resisted their retreat from the 1906 Calcutta resolutions.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q92

questions.q: The plan of Sir Stafford Cripps envisaged that after the Second World War
o: India should be granted complete independence
India should be partitioned into two before granting independence
India should be made a republic with the condition that she will join the Commonwealth
India should be given Dominion status
questions.e: The Cripps Mission (1942) offered India Dominion status after the war, with the right of provinces to stay out.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q93

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Famous place Region
1. Bodhgaya Baghelkhand
2. Khajuraho Bundelkhand
3. Shirdi Vidarbha
4. Nasik (Nashik) Malwa
5. Tirupati Rayalaseema
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Khajuraho is in Bundelkhand and Tirupati in Rayalaseema. Bodh Gaya is in Bihar, Shirdi is not in Vidarbha, and Nashik is not in Malwa.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q94

questions.q: The Parliament of India acquires the power to legislate on any item in the State List in the national interest if a resolution to that effect is passed by the
o: Lok Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
Lok Sabha by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its total membership
Rajya Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
Rajya Sabha by a majority of not less than two- thirds of its members present and voting
questions.e: Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha can empower Parliament to legislate on a State List subject by a resolution supported by two-thirds of members present and voting.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q95

questions.q: Recently, which of the following States has explored the possibility of constructing an artificial inland port to be connected to sea by a long navigational channel?
questions.e: Rajasthan proposed an artificial inland port at Jalore linked to the sea through a channel via the Kutch creek.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q96

questions.q:
With reference to the Agreement at the UNFCCC Meeting in Paris in 2015, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The Agreement was signed by all the member countries of the UN and it will go into effect in 2017.
2. The Agreement aims to limit the greenhouse gas emissions so that the rise in average global temperature by the end of this century does not exceed 2 °C or even 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels.
3. Developed countries acknowledged their historical responsibility in global warming and committed to donate $ 1000 billion a year from 2020 to help developing countries to cope with climate change.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Paris Agreement aims to keep warming well below 2 °C and pursue 1.5 °C. It came into force in 2016, not 2017, and the finance goal is USD 100 billion a year, not 1,000 billion.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q97

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sustainable Development Goals were first proposed in 1972 by a global think tank called the 'Club of Rome'.
2. The Sustainable Development Goals have to be achieved by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The SDGs came out of the 2012 Rio+20 conference and were adopted in 2015, to be achieved by 2030. The Club of Rome published 'Limits to Growth' in 1972, not the SDGs.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q98

questions.q: A recent movie titled The Man Who Knew Infinity is based on the biography of
questions.e: The 2015 film The Man Who Knew Infinity is based on the life of mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q99

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The minimum age prescribed for any person to be a member of Panchayat is 25 years.
2. A Panchayat reconstituted after premature dissolution continues only for the remainder period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The minimum age for Panchayat membership is 21 (Article 243F), not 25. A Panchayat reconstituted after early dissolution serves only the remainder of the term (Article 243E).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2016, GS Paper I, Q100
